feedback.problem: Find the projection of the intersection between the hyperboloid of two sheets $\frac{{x}^{2}}{2}-\frac{{y}^{2}}{4}+\frac{{z}^{2}}{4}=-1$ and the plane $y-2x=2$ onto the $xz$-plane.
feedback.worked_solution:
Since we want to find the projection onto the $xz$-plane, we need to eliminate the variable $y.$ First, we solve the equation of the plane for $y$, as follows:

$$
y-2x=2\,⟹\,y=2(x+1)
$$

Substituting the expression for $z$ into the equation of the hyperboloid, we obtain: 

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{{x}^{2}}{2}-\frac{(2(x+1))^{2}}{4}+\frac{{z}^{2}}{4} & =-1 \\ \frac{{x}^{2}}{2}-(x+1)^{2}+\frac{{z}^{2}}{4} & =-1 \\ \frac{{x}^{2}}{2}-{x}^{2}-2x-1+\frac{{z}^{2}}{4} & =-1 \\ -\frac{{x}^{2}}{2}-2x-1+\frac{{z}^{2}}{4} & =-1 \\ -\frac{{x}^{2}}{2}-2x+\frac{{z}^{2}}{4} & =0 \\ -\frac{{x}^{2}+4x}{2}+\frac{{z}^{2}}{4} & =0\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, by completing the square for the variable $x$, we have:

$$
\begin{aligned}-\frac{{x}^{2}+4x}{2}+\frac{{z}^{2}}{4} & =0 \\ -\frac{({x}^{2}+4x+4)-4}{2}+\frac{{z}^{2}}{4} & =0 \\ -\frac{(x+2)^{2}}{2}+2+\frac{{z}^{2}}{4} & =0 \\ \frac{(x+2)^{2}}{2}-\frac{{z}^{2}}{4} & =2 \\ \frac{(x+2)^{2}}{4}-\frac{{z}^{2}}{8} & =1\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the projection of the intersection is the hyperbola $\frac{(x+2)^{2}}{4}-\frac{{z}^{2}}{8}=1.$
